subject: physics
title: Rotational dynamics
key_idea: Rotation follows the same pattern as straight-line motion. Moment of inertia plays the part of mass, torque the part of force and angular momentum the part of momentum. Every straight-line equation has a rotational partner.

blocks.text: Moment of inertia measures how hard it is to change the rotation of an object. This section covers what sets its size.

items.meaning: How strongly an object resists a change in its rotation about a given axis. Unit: kg m².
The line the object turns about. I depends on which axis is used.

blocks.label: Moment of inertia of a point mass
Moment of inertia of an extended object
where: Add mr² for every small piece of the object.
Each piece has its own r from the axis.

blocks.text: Expressions for the moment of inertia of particular shapes are given in a question when they are needed.

items: A larger **mass** gives a larger I.
The way the mass is spread matters. Mass far from the axis adds much more than mass near it, because r is squared.
A hoop with all its mass at the rim has a larger I than a disc of the same mass and radius.
The same object has a different I about a different axis.
I = Σmr², so distance from the axis counts most.
I depends on the mass, how it is distributed and the axis chosen.
I is the rotational equivalent of mass.

blocks.text: A spinning object stores kinetic energy. A flywheel is a heavy wheel built to store it.

diagram.alt: A slider activity. Change the moment of inertia and the angular speed of a flywheel and read the energy it stores.

items: Energy stored rises with **I**, so a flywheel has a large mass concentrated near the rim.
Energy stored rises with **ω²**, so doubling the speed gives four times the energy.
The speed is limited by the strength of the material. The rim must not break apart.
**Smoothing torque and speed:** in a piston engine the torque is delivered in pulses. The flywheel absorbs energy during the power stroke and returns it between strokes, so the speed stays steady.
**Storing energy in vehicles:** a flywheel stores energy when the vehicle brakes and gives it back when it accelerates.
**Production machines:** a small motor spins a flywheel up slowly. The energy is then released in a short burst, for example to drive a press or punch.
Eₖ = ½Iω² depends on the square of the angular speed.
Storage capacity rises with I and with ω.
Flywheels smooth speed and torque, and store and release energy.

blocks.text: Angles replace distances. This section defines the quantities and gives the equations for uniform angular acceleration.

items.meaning: The angle turned through, in radians.
The rate of change of angle, in rad/s. It has size only.
Angular speed with a direction, the sense of the rotation.
The rate of change of angular velocity, in rad/s².

items: On an angle–time graph the gradient is the angular speed.
On an angular speed–time graph the gradient is the angular acceleration.
The area under an angular speed–time graph is the angle turned through.
A straight line on the ω–t graph means uniform angular acceleration. A curve means non-uniform angular acceleration.

blocks.label: The four equations
blocks.formula:
ω₂ = ω₁ + αt
θ = ((ω₁ + ω₂) ÷ 2)t
θ = ω₁t + αt² ÷ 2
ω₂² = ω₁² + 2αθ

items: Gradient of θ–t is ω. Gradient of ω–t is α. Area under ω–t is θ.
The four uniform-acceleration equations match v = u + at and the rest.
Each straight-line quantity has a rotational analogue.

sections.heading: Torque, angular momentum, work and power

blocks.text: Torque changes rotation. This section links torque to angular acceleration and angular momentum, then to work and power.

blocks.label: Torque from a force
where: r = perpendicular distance from the axis to the line of the force (m)

diagram.alt: A practice question. Work out the angular acceleration of a wheel from the torque and moment of inertia, with new numbers each time.
diagram.question: A resultant torque of {T} N m acts on a wheel of moment of inertia {I} kg m². Calculate its angular acceleration.

blocks.label: Angular momentum
where: Unit: kg m² s⁻¹ (kg m² rad/s)

items: Angular momentum is **conserved** when no external torque acts.
If I falls, ω must rise. A skater pulling in their arms spins faster.
A diver tucking in does the same, and spins faster in the air.
A torque acting for a time gives an **angular impulse**.

blocks.text: Rotating machinery always has frictional torque. The torque that accelerates the machine is the driving torque minus the frictional torque.

items: T = Fr and T = Iα. The resultant torque sets the angular acceleration.
Iω stays constant if no external torque acts.
W = Tθ and P = Tω. Frictional torque must be allowed for.

checks.q: A flywheel has moment of inertia 2.4 kg m² and turns at 150 rad/s. Calculate the energy it stores.
A resultant torque of 12 N m acts on a wheel of moment of inertia 0.60 kg m², starting from rest. Calculate its angular speed after 3.0 s.
A skater spins at 2.0 rad/s with moment of inertia 3.2 kg m². She pulls her arms in and her moment of inertia falls to 1.6 kg m². Calculate her new angular speed and explain why it changes.
checks.a: Angular momentum is conserved: 3.2 × 2.0 = 1.6 × ω, so ω = 4.0 rad/s. No external torque acts, so Iω is constant; when I falls, ω rises.
